rv.q: A decade on, the popular Mark Rylance still riding high after wowing audiences on both sides of the Atlantic in Jerusalem , is as good as ever and with strong support should guarantee a sell-out West End season for the Globe.
Casting and branding spell success for this West End transfer of a Bard double bill, but the inconsistent production makes the play itself feel only fitfully convincing.
This all-male production gave the plot’s who’s who the hilarity it deserves, and was nothing but a delight to watch.
Carroll’s production is ostensibly ebullient – this is, after all, a tragedy – but also catches the darker, deeper notes of cruelty and melancholy.

cn.t: Mark Rylance delivers a dazzling, award-worthy performance in this ebullient all-male production that successfully captures the Globe's collaborative spirit while balancing the play's humor and melancholy.
